finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /hooks/test sends a server-side HTTP POST to a fully attacker-controlled URL with no validation, allowing SSRF to internal services or cloud metadata endpoints. The response status is returned to the caller, which gives a port and host oracle.

trace.note: pub router handler for POST /hooks/test; no auth middleware is attached to the pub router, since requireAdmin is applied only to admin via admin.use at line 12
req.body.callback is passed directly to axios.post, which follows redirects by default and accepts any scheme or host
the upstream status code is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No URL parse, scheme or host allowlist, private/link-local IP blocking, or redirect restriction in this file. The only guard in the file, requireAdmin, is bound to the admin router and does not cover pub. I could not see how pub is mounted, because routes.js is the only file in the directory. Auth could exist at mount time, but nothing in the code I read enforces it. Ledger: admin GET /diagnostics/fetch (routes.js:15) is SAFE under the do-not-report rule, because requireAdmin (routes.js:7-12) is enforced and the attacker would need admin privilege.

verdict.reason: routes.js:20 passes req.body.callback straight into axios.post with no validation, and routes.js:12 applies requireAdmin only to the admin router, so the pub handler at routes.js:19 has no auth and the status is returned at routes.js:21. Mount-time auth for pub cannot be seen because routes.js is the only file, but nothing in the code enforces it.
